sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Austrotaxus spicata is a conifer endemic to New Caledonia's humid mid- and high-elevation forests. It grows as a shrub or tree up to about 25 m, with stiff leaves around 17 cm long in the local account. The seed is partly surrounded at maturity by an orange aril.

sections.title: Image and safety
sections.text: The plate shows a conifer with linear leaves and a fleshy seed covering, broadly consistent with the species; its fruit covering is described as orange, whereas the illustration appears red. Taxane alkaloids have been reported in Taxaceae leaves, but the cited evidence does not establish a human toxicity level for this species. No food use was verified.
